🤖 40 requests remain unfinished after 13 seconds, but pause fails on request identity


**What we did and why.** Repeated the one-engine Qwen3-0.6B queue measurement with the concurrency cap reduced from eight to four. The same 64 requests, frozen east model, 1,024-token forced outputs, sampling settings, native token-space client, two measured PPO delays and original five-second grace were retained. This tested whether the smaller cap could leave work for an actual pause/abort, before spending on another full training pair.

**Results.** The native test failed before the scheduler abort: `ValueError: native frontend includes an untracked request`. The task failed with exit 1, one attempt and no retry, after 227.815 seconds, costing 0.063281944444 H100 hours against the 0.166666666667-hour ceiling. The failure occurred in the identity ledger's strict subset check at the pause boundary.

The first read spanned 4.947766–4.951584 seconds after all admissions: 56 requests were unfinished, including 52 without a first token. The second read spanned 13.137458–13.141367 seconds: 40 were unfinished, including 36 without a first token. The separate pre-grace read still saw those 40. No successful native pause was recorded. Failure cleanup returned 36 logical results and canceled 28 logical tasks; each returned result contained 1,024 tokens and finite log probabilities, totaling 36,864 completed logical tokens. Cancellation is not eventual completion.

All 36 receipt chunks were retained and independently reassembled. Through the last pre-grace snapshot, the native ledger accounts for 64 starts, 24 length terminals containing 24,576 tokens and 40 active identities. It has no post-failure native drain. Consequently, neither full emitted-token conservation nor terminal resolution of all native requests can be established from this failed run. The measured protocol lasted 18.431902 seconds. This fixture had zero learner updates and no consumed training tokens, scorer or evaluation: training throughput, off-policy age, ESS, raw/contract-completed correctness and confidence intervals are not applicable. All 36 returned outputs intentionally reached the length limit; the other 28 logical tasks were canceled.

**What this means.** The lower concurrency leaves unfinished work at both observed PPO delays, but it also exposes an interface error hidden by earlier empty pause cohorts. In the pinned engine, the frontend dictionary is keyed by randomized internal request IDs. Each `RequestState` separately preserves the external request ID passed to generation. Our ledger tracks external IDs but passed internal dictionary keys to the subset check. The old CPU fake used identical keys and external IDs, so it missed this contract. Existing native receipts did not retain raw frontend IDs, preventing a retrospective internal/external join. We will not infer that join by stripping UUID suffixes or relax the ledger check.

**Next.** Run the separately reviewed repair using the explicit external request ID and retain both identities in the pause receipt. CPU checks now reproduce the original failure and pass the corrected boundary; the native repeat must still prove abort and completion accounting before the telemetry and pause-fix milestone.

🤖 Milestone 2: the evaluation and task MVP is in place

**What we did and why.** We built and qualified the existing-source evaluation system so later experiments can compare completed answers on a fixed, auditable question pool. It preserves native reward, checks binary correctness separately, and records an independent semantic score; the ranking metric requires both correctness and an accepted stop.

The frozen contract, pool, mechanical audit, split-safe sampler, paired harness, metric registry and native smoke gate are integrated. Difficulty ratings and power calibration continue alongside this scoped milestone. No language-model judge will be built under the September 9 ruling.

**Results.** Since the prior milestone:

- The [native evaluation check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5584832569) verified all **512 responses** at the two development endpoints: exact raw-reward mapping, correctness × accepted-stop, question membership and native/offline aggregate agreement. This is software qualification, with no treatment-effect interval.
- [Full Qwen ratings](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5589267597) audited **115,448 responses to 14,431 questions**. The resulting **1,918-question** calibration view has completed correctness **40.19% [39.19, 41.17]**. That interval is conditional on the observed selection and one engine seed. The two training anchors are now being audited for checkpoint-bound calibration; no minimum detectable effect has been claimed yet.
- The [Snowball loader precursor](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5588775164) completed **64 responses** with the bounded loader. A larger pilot is running; full Snowball difficulty ratings and training-task selection remain unfinished.

It does not establish equal quality.
- Engineering checks advanced independently: [ratio telemetry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5586086646), [optimizer telemetry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5587194050), and [background evaluation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5586317336) have audited results. 🤖 Eight controlled updates match training rewards across runners

### What we did and why

We compared synchronous training with the asynchronous runner restricted to zero rollout age, using Qwen3-0.6B. Both runners received the same prompt sets and request seeds, with matched communication settings before weight sync. This tests whether later comparisons can use the synchronous runner as their control (K4).

Each arm ran eight updates, with 64 prompts and four responses per prompt. We used seed 17 for the pair and seed 29 for an asynchronous repeat to measure variation. Evaluation was greedy on the same 128 development questions at startup and after training.

### Results

The seed-17 arms matched fingerprints of the consumed prompt-ID sets and raw training rewards at all eight updates. Both had zero rejected groups; the asynchronous runner consumed only age-zero rollouts. Every reward difference was therefore within the measured seed-repeat band.

Completed correctness counts answers that are correct under the task contract and finish with an accepted stop.

| Arm | Final completed correctness | Length stops | Consumed response tokens | Core training seconds | Task H100-hours |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Synchronous, seed 17 | 70/128 | 0/128 | 317,375 | 86.66 | 1.755 |
| Asynchronous, seed 17 | 68/128 | 1/128 | 317,375 | 123.90 | 1.901 |
| Asynchronous, seed 29 | 69/128 | 2/128 | 318,547 | 126.10 | 1.911 |

The full-ratio token effective-sample-size fraction ranged from 0.99875718 to 0.99901904 in both seed-17 arms and from 0.99874120 to 0.99900885 in the repeat. This measures importance-weight concentration on selected tokens.

Final asynchronous-minus-synchronous completed correctness was **−1.56 percentage points**, with a paired-question 95% interval of **[−7.03, +3.91] points**. Raw correctness equaled completed correctness at these endpoints. Semantic rescoring was unavailable for this legacy evaluation protocol.

Each seed-17 arm had one engine initialization failure caused by a port collision, followed by the runtime's built-in startup retry. All 50 observed worker processes, including failed and replacement starts, had the required settings. Scheduler retries and terminal telemetry export losses were zero. Total measured cost was 5.568 H100-hours.

### What this means

The prescribed control gate passes under these sampling and communication settings. The asynchronous runner was slower in this short, age-zero comparison. Core timing excludes startup and evaluation; this result does not rank production schedules.

The quality interval is conditional on the observed seed-17 models and is too wide to establish the 2-point non-inferiority claim. Consumed-set digests do not establish order within a batch. Earlier failed controls and the startup retries remain part of the record.

### Next

Integrate the qualified control, finish evaluation calibration, and complete the pause comparison needed for milestone 3, telemetry and pause fix landed. Quality-ranked sweeps will use the calibrated evaluation protocol.

🤖 Historical drift indicators do not establish a safe bound across 24 windows

**What we did and why.**

Before expanding the staleness ladder, this exploratory pilot (E4.5) tested whether existing indicators warned of the next decline in completed correctness. We reused six audited 100-update Qwen runs, all with training seed 17. Each prediction uses the preceding 20 updates and predicts the change between the current evaluation and the next one. This gives 24 dependent windows: five have a decline, and three decline by more than 2 percentage points.

The feature window, risk direction and two outcome definitions were fixed before calculating associations. Completed correctness uses the same audited verifier-plus-completed-stop endpoint as the historical reports. No new training ran. This informs the goal of faster Snowball training at the same answer quality.

**Results.**

| Indicator, fixed risk direction | AUROC: any next decline | AUROC: decline >2 pp |
|---|---:|---:|
| Lower legacy behavior-ratio ESS | 0.463 | 0.524 |
| Higher mean absolute log-ratio | 0.474 | 0.603 |
| Higher p99 absolute log-ratio | 0.442 | 0.619 |
| Higher mean squared log-ratio | 0.453 | 0.524 |
| Lower policy entropy | 0.547 | 0.619 |
| Higher raw gradient norm | 0.221 | 0.333 |
| Higher mean admitted age | 0.484 | 0.452 |

None of the available fixed-direction indicators reached AUROC 0.8 in this exploratory dataset. The whole-run bootstrap intervals are broad; for the primary endpoint, ESS is [0.159, 0.705], mean absolute log-ratio [0.206, 0.659], and low entropy [0.143, 0.798]. These intervals resample runs while retaining their dependent windows. They do not estimate variation across independent training seeds.

The existing ESS <0.5 flag never fired. A literal per-step mean-absolute-log-ratio >0.03 flag fired in two preceding windows; both were false alarms: 2/19, or 10.5%, for any subsequent decline. It missed all five declines. Applying the same threshold to each 20-update mean would erase both spikes, so that aggregation is reported separately.

The old worker absolute-log-ratio statistic is identically zero. Split stale-ratio ESS, split mismatch ESS, and gradient cosine are missing from these historical runs. In the new four-arm N1 correction screen, all 32 recorded stale-ESS values are exactly one, confirming that this particular statistic cannot discriminate rollout staleness when every batch has only one optimizer update.

All 7,800 native scalar values were recovered under exact run/job/region filters. Their 78 metric-family count/minimum/maximum/final summaries match the previous audited records in 312 checks. The pilot adds zero GPU-hours and zero optimizer updates; CPU analysis time was not separately benchmarked.

**What this means.**

The old indicators have not earned a predictive alert. The practical safe-bound rule is therefore closed for now: no predictive alert is adopted, and the ladders will be planned around the empirical quality knee. This is a design decision on the available evidence, not a universal statistical refutation. The held-out-seed AUROC ≥0.8 criterion remains untested; missing or structurally constant indicators remain untestable, not evidence of safety.

The legacy asynchronous behavior ratio combines engine mismatch and policy age. It must not be relabeled as either of the new split ratios. Type-A experiments need the actual split mismatch and age measurements; unit stale ESS in N1 is not a safe-bound signal. Health thresholds remain descriptive flags while the empirical quality knee and held-out-seed calibration determine the operating range.

**Next.**

Plan the staleness ladders around the empirical quality knee, with no predictive safe-bound alert. Keep the split-ratio and gradient-cosine telemetry and paired completed-score records so later held-out-seed evidence can reopen the rule. The next milestone is milestone 3, telemetry and pause fix landed.

Historical six-arm source: the audited Qwen family `2026.09.06.16`, legacy GSM8K development battery of 128 questions, greedy evaluation at 0/20/40/60/80/100. 🤖 Two dormant correction masks stay within the observed seed noise

**What we did and why.**

For the fresh-data correction check (K12 N1), we ran eight synchronous Qwen3-0.6B updates with one optimizer update per rollout batch: behavior clipping at seeds 17 and 29, plus the off-policy mask and M2 mask at seed 17. This checks that enabling either transform leaves fresh-data updates numerically well behaved before testing stale data, toward faster Snowball training at the same answer quality. All arms used the same frozen legacy GSM8K train/dev recipe, 64 prompts × 4 responses per update, and greedy evaluation on 128 fixed questions at updates 0 and 8. Completed correctness means verifier-correct with an accepted completion stop.

**Results.**

| Arm | Final raw / completed correct | Length stops | Consumed response tokens | Core seconds | Task H100-hours |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [Behavior clipping, seed 17](https://wandb.ai/dogml/marin-async-non-agentic-rl/runs/cbj0t3hi) | 70 / 70 of 128 | 4 / 128 | 316,946 | 79.330 | 1.606573 |
| [Behavior clipping, seed 29](https://wandb.ai/dogml/marin-async-non-agentic-rl/runs/erwlke3h) | 73 / 73 of 128 | 1 / 128 | 320,530 | 77.822 | 1.617778 |
| [Off-policy mask, seed 17](https://wandb.ai/dogml/marin-async-non-agentic-rl/runs/fhkcj239) | 72 / 72 of 128 | 3 / 128 | 317,920 | 78.919 | 1.619433 |
| [M2 mask, seed 17](https://wandb.ai/dogml/marin-async-non-agentic-rl/runs/wb97dzqc) | 69 / 69 of 128 | 3 / 128 | 318,745 | 78.571 | 1.632293 |

Both masks removed exactly zero tokens in the reported update metrics, and M2's pre-mask squared log-ratio statistic was zero. All four arms completed eight successful optimizer updates with positive gradients; each retained all 14 correction fields in both the batch aggregate and update-specific W&B records. The minimum raw gradient norm across the arms was 0.75685. These correction fields describe the last microbatch and rank mean; they are not token-pooled fractions for the whole update.

The frozen engineering noise band was the absolute difference between the two behavior-clipping seeds: 3/128, or 2.34375 percentage points. The off-policy mask differed from seed 17 by +1.5625 pp, with a paired 97.5% interval of [−4.6875, +7.8125] pp. M2 differed by −0.78125 pp, with [−8.59375, +7.03125] pp. Both meet the absolute noise-band rule. The intervals use 50,000 paired-question resamples and Bonferroni adjustment across these two contrasts for nominal 95% joint coverage, conditional on the observed training seeds.

The four runs used 6.476078 task H100-hours. All eight GPU tasks succeeded on their sole scheduler attempt. Retained hub logs contain no startup port-retry messages, but the incomplete telemetry coverage below prevents a whole-job zero-engine-death claim.

**What this means.**

The fresh-data numerical and final-score checks pass. This is an engineering check, not a non-inferiority result or a ranking of corrections. Zero masking here does not prove an active masking formula: the separate native numerical fixtures supplied that proof with nonzero retained gradients and actual parameter changes.

The full native telemetry audit is incomplete. The central query currently returns 23 of the expected 32 source-order events and eight of the expected 16 role-terminal receipts; every available terminal reports zero lost records. W&B and durable evaluation receipts cover all eight updates, but they cannot replace the missing complete source vectors and terminal counters. A direct regional query found neither the semantic training namespace nor its legacy parent namespace. This establishes a retrieval gap, not a correction or exporter failure. 🤖 Two training seeds differ by 8.61 points on completed heldout answers

**What we did and why.** We measured evaluation and training-seed variation
before using small-model experiments to choose faster Snowball training at
the same answer quality. Two Qwen anchors trained for 96 updates on the
frozen 1,918-question training view, then exported actual checkpoint weights.
Each checkpoint received five greedy passes on 256 development questions,
a separate greedy heldout pass, and separate stochastic panels with one,
four and eight draws on all 2,009 heldout questions.

**Results.**

| Anchor training seed | Heldout K8 completed | Pointwise 95% interval | Semantic correct / resolved | Semantic unresolved | Contract–semantic disagreements | Dev questions changing across five greedy passes |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 17 | 6,842 / 16,072 = 42.57% | 40.91–44.23% | 10,944 / 15,968 | 104 | 4,189 | 21 / 256 |
| 29 | 8,225 / 16,072 = 51.18% | 49.55–52.81% | 10,948 / 15,888 | 184 | 2,799 | 24 / 256 |

The paired difference is 8.61 percentage points, with a pointwise interval
of 7.56–9.65 points. These are large-question normal intervals conditional on
these two trained checkpoints, with each question's eight responses kept
together. They do not cover uncertainty over future training seeds.
The Platinum component contributes 2,606 versus 4,087 completed responses
out of 9,672; the MATH component contributes 4,236 versus 4,138 out of 6,400.

All 58,812 response rows across the two checkpoints passed exact native
token, request, renderer and contract-metric audits. Training, export and
calibration used 14.53 task H100-hours combined; evaluation alone used 0.635.

The balanced seed-by-question decomposition on the stochastic eight-draw
panel gives variance components 0.003688 for training seed, 0.112529 for
question, 0.013637 for their interaction and 0.121076 for draw residuals.
All raw estimates are positive. Seed variance has only one degree of freedom.

Under the explicit assumption that those marginal components apply equally
to two future arms, two training seeds and 2,009 questions with eight draws
give the following endpoint MDE planning sensitivity for the prespecified
45-contrast correction family, at 80% power and two-sided familywise 5% error:

| Assumed correlation of each component between future arms | Planning MDE |
| --- | ---: |
| −1 | 35.83 pp |
| 0, primary assumption | 25.34 pp |
| 0.5 | 17.92 pp |
| 0.9 | 8.01 pp |

The full artifact retains every componentwise correlation combination,
all raw and truncated moments, and the smaller prespecified comparison
families. These are normal planning approximations, not certified power
or confidence limits on the MDE. The endpoint calculation does not establish
power for a four-arm difference in age degradation.

**What this means.** The earlier rough five-point MDE is not supported by this
calibration under the stated assumptions. Similar development scores did
not predict heldout contract stability; the near-equal semantic totals and
large Platinum contract gap remain visible rather than being collapsed
into one quality score. Repeated greedy decoding also changed some answers.
The two-seed estimate is too uncertain to certify a two-point non-inferiority
claim, and the evaluation contract remains unchanged.

**Next.** Start the exploratory staleness calibration with matched control and
perturbation seeds to measure paired differences under its actual runner and
ordering. A large planning MDE does not stop that calibration; it limits which
rankings or quality guarantees the results can support. Snowball system
qualification and the frozen difficulty measurements continue independently.
The written disagreement sample remains available for review before any pool change.

🤖 Milestone 3: telemetry and the pause fix are integrated

**What we did and why.** We qualified request accounting and shorter pauses when syncing updated weights to rollout workers, so later experiments can measure asynchronous training without losing requests or confusing policy versions. The candidate completed twenty measured syncs on Qwen, using the earliest first-token policy version across partial rollouts. It also finished its final drain successfully.

Native optimizer remainder qualification (K29) landed: the synthetic two-GPU test saved about 4 retained bytes per owned parameter with BF16 moments and about 6 with moments plus remainders; all tested same-geometry checkpoint continuations were exact. Full-model memory and learning remain to be measured.

**Results.** The measured pause comparison was:

| Measurement | Recorded baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median pause | 5.100 s | 0.107 s |
| Median complete weight sync | 6.216 s | 1.211 s |
| Core time over twenty updates | 493.258 s | 433.487 s |

The candidate's pause p95 was 0.171 s and its maximum was 0.295 s, passing the median-below-0.3-second gate. All 29,344 started requests have terminal dispositions; eight engine identities stayed stable across the twenty measured syncs. These are descriptive timings from one matched configuration and seed, without an inferential timing interval. The baseline's failure during final cleanup remains recorded; its twenty measured syncs remain valid. The candidate changes both pause handling and admission-version selection, so the comparison does not isolate their individual effects or establish equal answer quality.

The candidate ended with 65/128 correct, completed development answers versus 71/128 in the baseline: a paired difference of −4.69 pp, 95% interval [−12.50, +3.13] pp. This question-resampling interval is conditional on one observed training seed and does not establish the two-point non-inferiority requirement. Both arms consumed 5,242,880 response tokens under the forced-length stress setup.

Since the evaluation and task milestone:

- The [seeded runner control](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5590472277) matched consumed prompt-set fingerprints and raw rewards at all eight updates. Its age-zero async arm was slower, and its completed-answer interval did not establish two-point non-inferiority.
- [Checkpoint calibration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5599222212) audited 58,812 responses. The two anchors differed by 8.61 pp [7.56, 9.65] on expected completed correctness across eight draws. That interval conditions on those checkpoints; the future-arm planning model's 25.34 pp minimum detectable effect exposes limited seed-level precision, with only one seed degree of freedom.
- The [full initial Snowball ratings](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5598262769), following the [pilot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5590578846), measured 40.24% [39.10, 41.37] completed correctness across 12,000 responses. This describes the selected 3,000-question panel at one checkpoint. Fresh ratings of the extremes and task selection are still underway.
- The [indicator pilot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5598170776) found no available fixed-direction indicator reaching AUROC 0.8 across its 24 dependent windows. No predictive alert is adopted; the ladders will locate the empirical quality knee.
- The [historical cadence reanalysis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5598140083) found lower core time at cadence four, but Snowball's completed-answer effects changed sign across seeds. Cadence, admission limits and token workloads changed together, so this does not isolate a cadence effect.
- The [fresh-data correction check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5598381936) found both masks dormant over eight updates, with no established quality benefit. Missing native source vectors and terminal receipts still prevent its full matched source-order qualification.
- The [eight-updates-per-batch correction diagnostic](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5599565967) demonstrated active masking with positive gradients and complete native coverage. Its averaged diagnostics are not whole-update token fractions, and it does not supply the missing matched quality comparison.
- The [same-host transport diagnostic](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5599467859) passed nine transfers and eighteen rank-level byte checks. Inter-host performance and equality of weights installed in the receiver model remain separate qualifications.

**What this means.** The request-accounting and pause changes are ready for this program's next asynchronous experiments. They remove the measured long pause without losing request dispositions in the qualified run. They do not establish Snowball speed, a safe off-policy age, or non-inferior quality. The calibration and indicator results make the confirmation work essential: uncertainty must be measured across training seeds, and constant or missing indicators cannot certify safety.

**Next.** Complete the fresh Snowball ratings and disagreement review, finish the reuse-ladder evaluations, and qualify receiver readback and inter-host transport for the next weight-sync improvements. The next milestone is **4, answer contract and tasks fixed**.

🤖 Nine payload pairs cross two physical hosts without byte errors

**What we did and why.** We qualified the production custom process-group path (K10 transport precursor) between two native Ray GPU actors on distinct physical hosts. This checks the transport mechanism needed for faster Snowball weight sync before loading a model or allocating its persistent buffers. The launcher repair supplies the immutable runtime root; the scientific packet remains three repeats at each of 32, 128 and 512 MiB, with aligned communicator settings and batch invariance off.

**Results.** Both tasks succeeded on their first attempts. The nine sender/receiver pairs produce 18 matching payload receipts, and each native rank checks every byte against its known pattern. Independent CPU replay recomputes all expected hashes. Both custom/default groups are destroyed, 30 origin-preserving stage events are retained, and both hosts report IB with GPU-direct RDMA.

| Payload | Repeat 1 | Repeat 2 | Repeat 3 | p50 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 MiB | 117.66948 ms | 2.05969 ms | 2.02811 ms | 2.05969 ms |
| 128 MiB | 7.48494 ms | 7.49673 ms | 7.26463 ms | 7.48494 ms |
| 512 MiB | 28.93216 ms | 28.72297 ms | 29.08819 ms | 28.93216 ms |

Each cell is the maximum of the two separately measured rank call durations.

Custom-group initialization takes 27.59909 and 27.56202 ms on the two actors. The per-rank clocks are independent; only each rank's elapsed duration is used. The receiver may enter its timed broadcast while the sender still constructs the payload, and the first collective includes cold initialization. These are observed call-wall durations, not an isolated fabric-bandwidth measurement or a model weight-sync estimate. Three repeats do not support a useful confidence interval, and no observation is excluded.

The two eight-H100 tasks both run for 205.482 seconds, totaling 0.9132533333333334 actual H100-hours. There are no updates, consumed training tokens, answer scores, age or ESS measurements in this model-free diagnostic. The previous two pre-measurement launcher failures remain recorded separately, with 0.6283866666666666 observed rank-0 H100-hours and unavailable rank-1 finish times.

**What this means.** Keep the production custom-group transport mechanism: distinct native hosts, symmetric settings, exact test-payload conservation and cleanup all pass. This establishes the transport precursor only. It does not prove full-model byte identity, receiver layout/headroom, packed-buffer performance or a Snowball speedup.

**Next.** Use the Snowball zero-update receiver readback to qualify the actual expert layout and available memory, then connect the bounded bucket implementation and frozen-sender byte replay. The next weight-sync milestone requires the full-model correctness and latency gates.

<details><summary>Provenance</summary>

The primary score averages completed correctness over eight stochastic responses per question and then equally across the two observed seeds; it is not best-of-eight.

**Results.** Two updates per batch achieved **46.22% completed correctness**, versus **15.49%** for one update. The paired difference is **+30.73 percentage points**, with conditional **98.75% interval [29.26, 32.21]**. The two seed-specific differences are +32.97 and +28.49 points. The development decline appears before the final checkpoint: the one-update runs fall from 151/256 and 152/256 completed answers at update 64 to 38/256 and 20/256 at update 96. Their final development truncation is 82.42% and 91.41%; both two-update runs finish at 168/256, with truncation 15.23% and 8.59%.

🤖 All 128 final responses hit the length limit in the importance-sampling run

## What we did and why

We audited the retained Snowball development responses from three 100-update runs to separate observable parser, stopping-configuration and repetition issues before testing remedies (E6.1 stage 1). This was a CPU analysis of existing data, covering 18 checkpoints and 2,304 responses. It launched no new training.

Each response was decoded with the pinned tokenizer and checked against its retained text and token hashes. We located the scorer's first numeric answer marker relative to the actual thinking-token state, including the prompt's opening state. The repetition diagnostic is the fraction of consecutive 16-token windows that duplicate an earlier window. The primary threshold is 0.5, with sensitivity checks at 0.25 and 0.75. These diagnostics overlap; they are not a partition of causes.

## Results

At update 100, the results were:

| Run | Responses at the length limit | First answer marker inside thinking, among length-limited responses | Repetition diagnostic ≥ 0.5, among length-limited responses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Weight sync every two updates, maximum age one | 63/128 | 58/63 (92.1%) | 62/63 (98.4%) |
| Weight sync every four updates, maximum age three | 25/128 | 19/25 (76.0%) | 24/25 (96.0%) |
| Every four updates, maximum age three, truncated importance sampling | 128/128 | 117/128 (91.4%) | 128/128 (100%) |

The older raw scorer rewarded 56, 16 and 113 length-limited responses in these three final checkpoints. Every one of those rewarded, length-limited responses had both its first answer marker inside thinking and a repetition diagnostic of at least 0.5. These are raw scorer outcomes, not completed-answer correctness.

The repetition finding persists across the prespecified sensitivity thresholds. At 0.25, all length-limited responses qualify. At 0.75, the counts are 41/63, 18/25 and 91/128. Across all final responses, first answer markers occur inside thinking in 123/128, 122/128 and 117/128; the parser issue is therefore also present outside the length-limited subset.

The effective EOS configuration was present for all three runs. The pinned backend defaults to respecting EOS, uses tokenizer EOS 128001, and adds generation-config EOS 128009. Executing its actual configuration-update method reproduces that effective stop set; switching `ignore_eos` on removes both stopping conditions. An empty explicit stop-token list does not establish a missing EOS stop set. This is a configuration diagnostic, not a causal explanation of individual truncations.

## What this means

The raw scorer can reward an answer marker still inside thinking, including responses that repeat until their length limit. Repetition and answers parsed inside thinking frequently coexist. The audit cannot assign either as the sole cause of truncation, and it does not establish that EOS configuration was broken.

The evidence uses finalized trajectory tokens. It does not reconstruct unavailable raw engine outputs. These deterministic development responses describe the observed runs; they do not estimate training-seed uncertainty or held-out quality, and they do not qualify a remedy.

## Next

Prepare the prescribed short Snowball remedy comparison: parser correction alone and its combinations with forced thinking closure, the two truncation penalties, and repetition stopping. Preserve the existing stopping settings unless an effective-configuration defect is demonstrated. Stage 2 remains necessary for milestone 4; this CPU audit does not complete that milestone or establish non-inferiority.

The optional grouped-allocation attribute was unavailable; that separate optimization remains unqualified. InfiniBand evidence is retained in bounded log tails, including GDRDMA lines for 34 processes, rather than a complete fabric trace.

**Next.** Run one packed installation and an untimed full frozen-source byte replay, retaining complete sender/receiver coverage and measured additional allocation. Each arm made eight optimizer updates; a separate second-moment diagnostic used eight minibatches from one larger rollout batch. This is class R research: the correction-selection experiment decides eventual use (K12).

Second-moment masking differs by −1.953125 pp, CI [−7.03125, 3.125], and fails it. These question-bootstrap intervals condition on the observed seed, use 50,000 draws and cover the two candidate comparisons; they do not establish non-inferiority or a population-level seed effect.

Every arm consumed 512 distinct prompt groups. The matched seed-17 arms use the same source-group union, but generated responses and token counts differ. The diagnostic establishes that masking can activate, not that it improves quality.

🤖 Seeded release thresholds leave mean training age unchanged at 3.0

**What we did and why.** We tested whether deliberately holding generated prompt groups makes training consume older responses, a prerequisite for measuring how staleness affects faster Snowball training at the same answer quality (K17). Two Qwen3-0.6B arms used the same seed, eight updates, FIFO admission, publication every four updates, an age limit of six, a 256-group buffer and 64 generation workers. One arm had no injected delay; the other set each prompt’s release threshold to its first-token admission step plus a reproducible integer from zero to three. This threshold may already have passed when generation finishes; it does not guarantee additional waiting after completion. Admission order and delay are class T tradeoffs: this test does not select a default.

**Results.**

| Arm | Updates | Consumed tokens | Core s | Task H100 h | Final completed | Semantic | Eval truncation % | Group age mean / p95 | Stale ESS range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---|---|
| FIFO, no injected delay | 8 | 433,471 | 63.12 | 1.737556 | 107/256 (41.80%) | Not separately scored | 3.91 | 3.0 / 6 | 1.0000 |
| FIFO, seeded delay 0–3 | 8 | 434,728 | 64.60 | 1.979604 | 106/256 (41.41%) | Not separately scored | 5.08 | 3.0 / 6 | 1.0000 |

The frozen capability requirement was a positive increase in mean group age. The observed increase is **0.0 updates, so that gate fails**. Both arms have the identical age histogram: 64 groups at each age 0, 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, and 128 at age 3. Each consumed 320 groups older than two updates. Token-weighted mean ages are 3.2300 and 3.1455, respectively; these also do not show an increase from delay.

The delay mechanism itself executed: the 512 consumed groups received delays 0/1/2/3 in counts 150/140/107/115. Every consumed UID joins to its seeded assignment and first-token admission stamp; no group was released before its assigned real update, and no consumed age exceeded six. Both arms generated 832 groups: 512 consumed, 64 cancelled before enqueue and 256 discarded at epoch end, with zero stale discards and complete token conservation. Under this schedule, delay changed which prompts entered batches without changing the consumed policy-age cohorts.

Completed correctness is full credit from the task's own scorer multiplied by an accepted stop, computed from the final 256 retained response records. Descriptive endpoint Wilson 95% intervals are 35.92–47.92% and 35.54–47.52%. These reused development questions had a 1,024-token response limit. The two endpoints are descriptive; no paired quality superiority, non-inferiority or default-selection test was performed.

The displayed stale ESS compares the training forward pass with the pre-update current-policy forward pass. With one optimizer update per batch, its value of one does not establish that old rollout behavior matches the current policy. The separate current-policy-versus-rollout ESS ranges are 0.99656–0.99927 and 0.99686–0.99933; those comparisons combine age and inference-engine effects rather than isolating either one.

All four original physical tasks succeeded, costing 3.717160 H100 hours. The audit joins 6,768 native/W&B scalars, 16 exact source digests and all eight role-terminal records, with zero lost or queued records. All 16 native core phase durations match W&B within 8.9e-16 seconds of JSON round-off. Core time includes buffer wait, training and scheduled weight publication, excluding evaluation, checkpoint callbacks and startup; generation overlaps this window. These are two recordings of the same timer, not independent clocks or a matched-token speed comparison.

**What this means.** Keep the failed positive-shift result unchanged and leave the delay capability unqualified. Mechanical release correctness is established, but it does not establish the intended age shift. This pair also does not resolve the larger staleness ladder: its publication cadence and common buffer geometry differ from that fleet, and it has no held-out quality comparison.

comments.author: atqamar
comments.body:
🤖 Post-thinking scoring lowers completed correctness by 14.23 pp on retained Snowball responses

**What we did and why.** We rescored the same retained Snowball responses using the answer after the thinking boundary, while preserving their original rewards, stop reasons and semantic scores. This checks whether the earlier task ratings support the corrected answer contract needed for faster training at the same answer quality. The task-rating diagnostic (E6.2) uses existing responses; it generates no new answers.

**Results.** Completed correctness requires both a correct answer and an accepted stop. The later sample contains questions selected as extremes under the original ratings and is reported separately.

| Retained population | Questions / responses | Original completed | Post-thinking completed | Paired change, pp (95% interval) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Original four draws per question | 3,000 / 12,000 | 4,829 / 12,000 (40.24%) | 3,121 / 12,000 (26.01%) | −14.23 [−15.06, −13.41] |
| Later eight draws on legacy-selected extremes | 1,025 / 8,200 | 1,898 / 8,200 (23.15%) | 1,235 / 8,200 (15.06%) | −8.09 [−8.96, −7.24] |

Intervals resample paired questions and condition on the observed responses and selection. The samples are never pooled as twelve draws. Semantic results, including unresolved cases, are unchanged.

Artificially cutting retained responses at 4,096 tokens gives completed rates of 25.03% and 13.98%, respectively. These are censored-prefix diagnostics: they do not reproduce generation with a shorter context or a force-close/repetition intervention. This CPU-only analysis adds no training updates or GPU hours.

**What this means.** Class R: the task-rating experiment decides the training pool. The original ratings materially overstate completed correctness under the post-thinking rule, so they cannot qualify the corrected pool. This is a scoring comparison on identical responses, not a model-quality decline or an estimate of intervention efficacy. Pool adoption remains undecided.

**Next.** Qualify the native answer interventions and obtain fresh ratings under the actual corrected serving settings. That evidence, together with the disagreement spot-check, is needed for the next milestone, “answer contract and tasks fixed.”

comments.body: 🤖 Correction after tracing the current checkpoint path: the long-lived `GlobalAsyncCheckpointManager` keeps the completed TensorStore commit futures in `_commit_futures`; `wait_until_finished()` joins but does not clear them, and the writes allow indefinite source-buffer references. PR #8599 contained a reviewed post-join cleanup for these futures, but that part did not land with #8609.
